title: Vertical Compression of an Inverse-Square Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Give an equation for the graph of y = 1 + 1 / x^2 after it is compressed vertically by a factor of 2.

steps.title: Recall the Vertical Compression Rule
steps.explanation: To compress the graph of y = f(x) vertically toward the x-axis by a factor of c > 1, divide the entire function f(x) by c (or multiply by 1/c).
steps.why: Vertical compression by a factor of c multiplies every y-coordinate by 1/c.

steps.title: Multiply the Function by 1/2
steps.explanation: Multiply the entire right-hand side 1 + 1/x^2 by 1/2.
steps.why: Setting c = 2 scales all vertical outputs by 1/2.

steps.title: Distribute the Factor 1/2
steps.explanation: Distributing 1/2 across both terms yields y = 1/2 + 1/(2x^2), shifting the horizontal asymptote from y = 1 to y = 1/2.
steps.why: Distributing 1/2 scales each additive term of the function.
